reviews.summary: WP1 fails because ordinary calls can leave an ended emitter sounding, keep a selected emitter silent, or cut a voice off in one frame during an eight-frame fade. The native buffer and import-free WebAssembly module agree on the reference samples, and the full-pool cost is within real time on both. Five items pass and six fail.

findings.name: Repeated plays can keep a pending master mute from reaching the mix
findings.different: The previous listener-write case now delivers its emitter. Play bypasses the retry priority and repeatedly takes the free slot ahead of an already pending volume change.

findings.name: Holding a fading-in emitter makes it grow louder
findings.different: The earlier emitter findings concerned a radius exit, stereo routing and ending a restored emitter. This hold interrupts the entry glide of an unplaced mono loop.

findings.name: Holding during a volume reduction exceeds the ramp step
findings.different: The previous stop and displacement defect at PCM exhaustion is fixed. This is a continuing loop whose volume glide and hold envelope both fall during the same frames.

findings.name: Fully held emitters still incur per-frame rendering work

reviews.summary: WP1 fails three of its eleven items. A master mute stayed pending for three seconds while the mix accepted every play, and holding a loop during a gain change broke its fade to silence. The eleven findings in the previous review are fixed in their reported cases. A separate per-frame cost remains for emitters held at silence.

findings.name: An emitter restored on resume can keep sounding after it ends
Releasing a restored emitter can leave it held
findings.different: The prior hold during entry now fades correctly. Here the post-resume release command is discarded and the selected loop stays silent.

findings.name: An emitter volume changed while the queue is full can be lost on resume
findings.different: The earlier master mute now reaches the mix during continuous plays. This emitter change reaches the queue once, is rejected at the restored snapshot revision and is never retried.

reviews.summary: WP1 fails three of eleven items. After an interruption, one play can cause the mix to discard an emitter’s latest change permanently. At the default queue capacity, an ended loop still rendered at 0.125 in both channels after 4,096 frames and eight further updates, while the handle reported zero emitters.
